name: Bambaroo with a Twist!
description:
We're having a one day walk on Sunday that will take in the bottom section of the Bambaroo Track, but once we get to the beautiful trees we're going to put a twist into the day and venture towards Insulator Creek and check out a couple of magical waterfalls.  

If you're not already on our mailing list contact the Club directly by email (tsvbush@hotmail.com) to find out all the details and who to contact to nominate for the walk. 

Hope to see you Sunday on a Track.

name: Echo Creek and K Traverse
description:
Next Walk Sunday May 30 

Echo Creek & K Track, Paluma.   

Leader Luen Warneke.  To register or for more info 0415 947 748 or luenwarneke@gmail.com 

Meeting Place: Paluma Village Green @ 8 am.  

This Sunday we will go faraway in time to Echo Beach rather I mean Creek.   Luen will lead us on yet another creek based adventure.  If it is anything like the Cloudy/Ethel adventure we will experience beautiful forest country; very attractive creek scenery; be in the creek as part of the scenery enjoying the anti-inflammatory properties of the creek (i.e. over knee deep in water).  There will no doubt be parts where there will be out of creek off track walking and need to divide a way for ourselves via wait-a-while.   


The plan is very loose: we’ll meet in Paluma and drove to the Dam road and park at the start of the K-Track, walk to the headwaters of Echo Creek and follow the creek downstream.  As indicated earlier you will most likely get your feet wet, so choose your footwear wisely.  You don’t want to wear anything that will slip when wet.  We will be in and out of the creek, finding the best route possible.  As always there will be rainforest plants involved so be prepared to divide a way through it (seceteurs).  We’ll stop for morning tea, lunch and hopefully afternoon tea.   Once we’ve had enough of the creek we’ll rejoin the K-track and follow it back to the cars.  We’ll be back at the cars between 3 and 5 pm.    

Bring your hat, sunscreen, insect repellent & shoes that you don’t mind getting wet.  Long sleeved shirts are recommended to protect yourself from scratches and the sun.  Some people wear long pants, others shorts with gaiters: the choice is yours.   

First aid kit, snake bandage, water 2 – 3 L.  Refill from the creek, but it is also an idea to bring water purification tablets.  If you’re not happy with drinking creek water – treated or not - bring 4 L for the day.  Morning tea, lunch, afternoon tea.  Other snacks.  Gifts and other tributes for walk leader and any of the committee members who happen to be on the walk.  Camera, togs & towel.  Change of clothes for the journey home is a good idea.  Even if not car pooling you could be soaked and getting into clean dry clothes is really nice at the end of a walk.   

It is wise to bring a dry bag to put store the gear you’ll take on the walk that you do not want to get wet.   

Visitors must pay a $5 visitor fee and sign an acknowledgement of risk form.  You must be over 18 to participate.   

For gleam more information and details on the walk & to register for it please contact Luen directly.

name: Cloudy Creek and Ethel Creek
description:
Sunday 16th May – Another Luen-Led Adventure
Cloudy and Ethel Creek Explore (Paluma area). Off-track rainforest creek exploration. 
Leader – Luen. To register or for more info contact the walk leader
Type of walk – half to full day exploration bushwalking. Walk will be around ~10+ km. Track at start and end of day – but will be several hours off-track exploring the creeks and walking through rainforest, viewing lovely creek scenery. Route map: https://maps.wanderstories.space/?id=1620711096583#-19.00408,146.1967,15z,outdoor,alertsQld/articles
In Brief: Walk on Collins' Track to where it meets and crosses Cloudy Creek, then go down stream to Cloudy Creek Falls (off track). Walk on-track to Ethel Creek Falls. Walk up stream along Ethel Creek and then off-track to the Paluma Ewen Road. Walk back along the road to the village. 

This wonderful walk will start and end in Paluma village.  The tracks that will be used at various stages of this walk (Collins’ and the Paluma-Ethel Falls Tracks) pass through very scenic rainforest terrain; the off-track portion, particularly down Crystal Creek is straight through the rainforest, where Luen will be busy looking for the best route.  This is what off-track is all about.  Be aware it could be a little bit overgrown in places and there may be some thorns, etc., from various vines and other shrubs, hence the need for some protective clothing.  It may be necessary at times to walk in the creek itself, so wet feet are a definite possibility.  Ethel Creek Falls is quite spectacular and makes a great backdrop for a photograph; Did we mention its also a great swimming spot?  Well it is, just what tired bodies need.  After this we’ll be going through the forest (off-track) to get back to the main road.  You will WALK back to Paluma village because no self-respecting driver would stop for a rag tag bunch like us: so no thumbs out to try and hitch a lift back you slackers.  

Cost – non-members $5 fee. 
 
What you need – carry water (minimum 2 lt), refill from creek as required (treat / filter your water refill).  Due to our proximity to Paluma Village we never can be 100% sure about the water, so we do recommend that if you are comfortable drinking straight from the creek you bring something to treat the water.  Tablets like iodine or chlorine, or even a filter should work fine.  The alternative is to bring about 4 L for the whole day.  

Lunch,  snacks / energy food, electrolytes, hat, sunscreen, insect repellent (to keep the leeches & mozzies at bay), enclosed sturdy footwear, personal first kit. Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves. Hiking poles are good on track walks and sometimes when crossing creeks; on off-track sections they are probably best secured in your pack.  
 
Note – footwear will get wet, so wear foot wear that is suitable.  
 
Timing and meet – Meet Paluma Village Green at the car park near the toilet block at 8 am. 
Estimated Completion – back at the car park around 2-5 pm depending on group size, how  long we spend off track (due to vegetation/terrain), amount of breaks, and fitness levels.
 
Must be over 18yrs to participate.  It’s not that we don’t like youngsters, but visitors are considered temporary members and to be a member you have to be over 18.  

In addition Luen must approve your registration for the walk – if he thinks based on the information you provide him or based on the types of walks you’ve done that this isn’t the best option for you, he has the right veto your nomination.  This is a safety precaution the Club takes.
